penalties_applied.name: b2c_at_scale_needed
penalties_applied.reason: Shared-hosting customers are individual consumers or tiny businesses paying $5–15/month for hosting. A bot-blocking micro-SaaS at any meaningful price point ($5-20/mo) would need hundreds of paying customers to generate viable revenue, requiring B2C scale that a solo operator cannot achieve through targeted outreach.

rationale: The pain is real and recurring, and the technical solution (generating htaccess rules or a Cloudflare config) is very buildable with Claude. The problem is commercial: shared-hosting customers are individual consumers who already pay very little for hosting and have low willingness to pay for security add-ons, especially when free alternatives (Cloudflare's free tier, Wordfence for WordPress users) exist. The buyer is too vague — 'small business owner on shared hosting' spans millions of people with wildly different contexts and no single reachable channel — and the business model requires consumer scale that a solo operator cannot drive.
solution_plan: The technical build is genuinely easy: a Claude-powered form where a user describes their hosting setup and gets a tailored .htaccess bot-blocking ruleset emailed to them, paid via a one-time Stripe link ($9-19). The factory could build this in days. However, reaching paying customers is the unsolvable problem: there is no B2B channel, no high-intent list, and no clear reason for shared-hosting customers (who already have free options) to pay. Without a distribution edge, this sits as a free blog post or a tiny Gumroad product, not a sustainable micro-SaaS. Not recommended for this factory.
notes: Fails willingness_to_pay floor (4 < 5) and buyer_clarity floor (4 < 6). Total also below validate threshold after penalty.
